description: RC1 (PRIMARY, must be first and independent) — restore ovms-embeddings availability. The actual outage: all four replicas sit 0/1 because the live inline '-m 2 ping' readiness probe cannot survive a wedged/RET_CHECK serving path, and OmniRoute load-balances onto dead backends returning 'fetch failed'. Fix: create the missing ovms-readiness-scripts ConfigMap, reconcile its embed-probe.sh to the endpoint that actually serves a 1024-dim vector on a healthy replica, and roll in the gentler script probe (timeout 5s / failThresh 4 / period 15s) + the embeddings memory bump to 12Gi, ONE replica at a time via the StatefulSet rollingUpdate.partition (3->2->1->0). This also folds in the RC4 embeddings memory bump (8Gi->12Gi) because it ships in the same StatefulSet reconcile. Independent of the ceiling and model-id work. Keep model-pull at --max_length=4096 for THIS feature (the ceiling bump is FEAT-003).
steps: Re-run the design F7 checklist over SSH BEFORE any mutation: capture embeddings/reranker memory limit, embeddings readiness probe shape, graph max_length, whether cm ovms-readiness-scripts exists, OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB, and qdrant StatefulSet revision; and do a fresh per-replica 1-token ping to find which ordinal is currently healthy (health rotates). Record these in findings.

Determine the serving endpoint: on a HEALTHY replica, POST a 'ping' to both http://localhost:8000/v1/embeddings and /v3/embeddings and confirm which returns HTTP 200 with a 1024-dim 'embedding' array. The live inline probe uses /v1; the committed embed-probe.sh uses /v3. Pick the one that serves 1024 dims.

Edit ~/sources/kube/omniroute-memory/ovms-readiness-scripts-configmap.yaml on the remote host so embed-probe.sh posts to the confirmed serving endpoint (keep EXPECTED_DIM=1024, TIMEOUT=4). Then apply it: kubectl -n omniroute-memory apply -f ~/sources/kube/omniroute-memory/ovms-readiness-scripts-configmap.yaml (it is NotFound live, so the pod cannot mount the script until this exists).

Edit ~/sources/kube/omniroute-memory/ovms-embeddings-statefulset.yaml on the remote host: keep the committed script-based readinessProbe (/opt/readiness/embed-probe.sh, timeoutSeconds 5, failureThreshold 4, periodSeconds 15); set resources.limits.memory to 12Gi; replace the stale ceiling-formula memory comment with the +50%/12Gi directive rationale; leave model-pull args at --max_length=4096 for this feature.

Set the rolling-update partition so ONLY the highest-ordinal pod rolls first: kubectl -n omniroute-memory patch sts ovms-embeddings --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/updateStrategy/rollingUpdate/partition","value":3}]'. Then apply the reconciled StatefulSet. Watch ovms-embeddings-3 for a bounded 10-minute window.

If pod-3 reaches and HOLDS READY >=10 min with no climbing restarts, lower the partition stepwise (2, then 1, then 0), waiting for each pod to hold READY before the next. After the last pod is READY, reset partition to 0 (or remove it).

If a rolled pod does NOT recover (wedge or RET_CHECK persists under the gentler probe), STOP before rolling the rest. Run the single-pod CPU canary via the partitioned roll (target_device: CPU on one replica) to localize GPU-vs-CPU: a device change MUST be proposed to the user via send_message (warning) before applying. On any pod failing its 10-min window, run kubectl -n omniroute-memory rollout undo statefulset ovms-embeddings and restore the prior partition.
Throughout: confirm the qdrant StatefulSet revision is unchanged. Do not apply the reranker manifest here.
acceptance_criteria: ovms-embeddings holds >=3/4 replicas READY continuously for >=10 minutes with no climbing restarts and zero Unhealthy events (design AC1, AC3).
Public POST /v1/embeddings with arc-embed/qwen3-embedding-0.6b returns HTTP 200 + a 1024-dim vector across 20 consecutive calls with no 'fetch failed' (design AC2).
cm ovms-readiness-scripts exists in ns omniroute-memory and the embedding pods mount it; embed-probe.sh targets the endpoint that serves a 1024-dim vector.
Embeddings container resources.limits.memory reads 12Gi (design AC6 embeddings portion).
qdrant StatefulSet revision is unchanged (design AC8).
verification: ssh -o BatchMode=yes celes@192.168.42.254 'kubectl -n omniroute-memory get pods -l app=ovms-embeddings -w' — observe >=3/4 READY held >=10 min, restart counts stable.
ssh ... 'kubectl -n omniroute-memory get sts ovms-embeddings -o jsonpath="{..containers[?(@.name==\"ovms\")].resources.limits.memory}"' — expect 12Gi.

Public API: 20x POST https://omniroute.celestium.life/v1/embeddings (bearer /run/secrets/omniroute_management_api_key) model arc-embed/qwen3-embedding-0.6b input 'ping' — all HTTP 200, 1024 dims, no fetch failed.
ssh ... 'kubectl -n omniroute-memory get cm ovms-readiness-scripts' — exists.
ssh ... 'kubectl -n omniroute-memory get sts <qdrant-sts> -o jsonpath="{.metadata.generation}"' before/after — unchanged.
blocked_reason: FLOOD SOURCE IDENTIFIED = an EXTERNAL client, not the GPUs or kube. After B+C were applied (OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS=4096, OVERFLOW=auto, OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=12288 via kubectl set env on the omniroute deploy; nginx proxy scaled to 4 nodes with max_fails=1/fail_timeout=15s/proxy_next_upstream failover), the GPUs STOPPED erroring (PF ccs0/fence delta=0 over idle windows) — so they are NOT flooding with hardware errors anymore. BUT all 4 PF nodes stay SATURATED/slow (tiny-call latency 4-8s vs healthy 0.04s) because an external API client (x-omniroute-auth-id key_a784, auth-kind client_api_key) is CONTINUOUSLY posting LARGE documents to /v1/embeddings: of the last 59 arc-embed calls, 51 were >4096 tokens (observed 7036, 8740, 9089, 9940, 10432, 10605 tokens), each taking 30-40s on the Arc GPU. These large single ITEMS are NOT being chunked to <=4096 by OMNIROUTE_EMBEDDING_SPLIT_MAX_ITEM_TOKENS (that guard splits multi-item BATCHES and, per the image docs, with overflow=auto an over-cap item from an EXTERNAL caller should get HTTP 400 — yet 10k-token items still reach OVMS, so either the guard is not enforcing single-item size for this path or the client sends them in a way that bypasses the split). Net: the 'flood' is real external embedding demand for big documents, and the Arc PF can serve them but only slowly (30-40s each), keeping the fleet pegged. This is the honest answer to the user's 'are we still flooded?' — not GPU error-flooded, but LOAD-saturated by an external big-document client. REMAINING DECISION (product-level, not mine to make): either (a) actually enforce a hard per-item reject/truncate at 4096 for this provider (would make that client's >4096 inputs fail or be clipped — behavior change the client sees), (b) accept 30-40s large-embedding latency as the cost of serving big documents on this hardware, (c) add real concurrency/queue limiting so big items don't pile up, or (d) the deeper GPU driver/firmware (DKMS/GuC) bump for faster large-item compute. host-native PF topology + proxy failover are DONE and correct; qdrant untouched (gen=1 uid a2c81b89). PRIOR: ALL-4-NODE HOST-NATIVE DEPLOYED + OMNIROUTE ROUTED, but a NEW honest limit surfaced: the Meteor Lake Arc GPUs wedge on the PF too (not just the VF) under OmniRoute's HEAVY real retrieval load, and the wedge ROTATES across whichever node absorbs the load. STATUS: (1) Host-native OVMS runs on all 4 gremlins (shared NixOS module modules/ovms-embeddings-host.nix via common.nix, podman, PF /dev/dri/renderD128, port 8000, model max_length=8192, runtime-resolved video GID; commits 4b2a931/260de4a on branch dev). All 4 serve 1024-dim and pass light/moderate load cleanly (gremlin-1/4 did 5/5-8/8 clean, 0 PF errors, ~40ms). (2) The in-cluster ovms-embeddings StatefulSet was SCALED TO 0 (reversible; object kept) to free the GPUs from the VF-wedging pods per the user's 'get off kube' direction. (3) OmniRoute routing: OmniRoute reaches arc-embed via the ovms-embeddings Service DNS (ovms-embeddings.omniroute-memory.svc:8000, path /v3/embeddings, confirmed from call_logs). Direct ClusterIP->node-IP endpoints hit a kube-proxy hairpin (pod->own-node-host fails ~25-50%), so I deployed an in-cluster nginx reverse-proxy Deployment (ovms-embeddings-proxy, hostNetwork, listen :8001, upstream all four 10.1.1.12-15:8000 with proxy_next_upstream failover) and pointed the ovms-embeddings Service at the proxy. hostNetwork fixed the hairpin; from a pod the Service served 30/30 clean when backends were healthy, and OmniRoute backend call_logs flipped to status:200. THE REMAINING BLOCKER: under OmniRoute's real retrieval traffic (which includes ~4596-token requests taking ~300s), the Arc PF compute path wedges with the SAME ccs0 'Unexpected memirq status 0x0' + 'Fence expiration time out i915-0000:00:02.0:ovms' signature seen on the VFs — just needs more sustained compute to trigger on the PF. It rotates: whichever node gets the heavy load wedges (observed gremlin-2, then gremlin-3, then gremlin-1 in turn), recovers when load shifts or on a container restart / node reboot. nginx fails over to healthy backends so 3/4 usually serve, but paced public /v1/embeddings AC2 still shows 5-7/12..15 client timeouts under load (NOT 'fetch failed' — slow/hanging, not refused). So small/public calls succeed (verified: a tiny public call returned 200 + a valid embedding in ~3s), but sustained heavy load is not clean. i915.reset=1+request_timeout_ms=10000 (gremlin-2 only, from the earlier reboot) did NOT prevent its PF wedge. CONCLUSION: host-native PF is strictly better than VF/kube (no permanent 0/4 outage, light load clean, failover works) but does NOT fully cure the Arc ccs0 fence-timeout hang under heavy compute. NEEDS a decision: (a) apply i915.reset=1 fleet-wide via reboot of gremlin-1/3/4 (gremlin-2 has it) and re-measure; (b) cap OmniRoute per-item tokens / concurrency so no single request pushes the GPU into the multi-hundred-second regime that triggers the wedge; (c) scale proxy to all 4 nodes; (d) accept 3/4-with-failover as the operating point; or (e) a deeper GPU driver/firmware remediation (DKMS/GuC bump). qdrant untouched throughout (gen=1 uid a2c81b89 1/1). PRIOR CANARY/REPOINT NOTES: CANARY SUCCEEDED on serving, BLOCKED on the OmniRoute repoint plumbing. Host-native OVMS on the MASTER/PF Arc device (gremlin-1, /dev/dri/renderD128, PCI 0000:00:02.0) serves arc-embed CLEANLY under sustained load: 40/40 then 10/10 clean 1024-dim responses, ~40ms steady latency, token sweep serves up to 7500 words (past 4096) at 13.6s, and ZERO ccs0 memirq errors / fence timeouts on the PF (00:02.0) during load. This DEFINITIVELY proves the ccs0 compute hang is specific to the SR-IOV VF compute path; the physical function does not wedge. The host service runs the same openvino/model_server image + qwen3-embedding-0.6b model, graph max_length=8192 (ceiling goal baked in), via a NixOS systemd/docker service on gremlin-1 only. REMAINING BLOCKER (step 5 repoint): OmniRoute's arc-embed provider backend URL is 'http://ovms-embeddings.omniroute-memory.svc.cluster.local:8000/v3/embeddings' (confirmed from a call_log) and is stored in OmniRoute's sqlite DB (/app/data/storage.sqlite), NOT in env or a configmap, so it cannot be repointed via kubectl set env; it needs either an OmniRoute admin-API/UI provider edit or a live DB edit (risky). Also, pointing the in-cluster ovms-embeddings Service at the PF host IP (10.1.1.12:8000) via a selectorless Service + manual EndpointSlice WORKS but is only ~50% reliable because kube-proxy hairpins a ClusterIP->node-own-IP endpoint (worst case: the omniroute pod runs ON gremlin-1, the same node as the PF endpoint). Direct host-IP access from the omniroute pod is 100% reliable (~1ms), so repointing OmniRoute's provider URL DIRECTLY to http://10.1.1.12:8000/v1/embeddings (bypassing the ClusterIP) is the clean fix — but needs the OmniRoute provider-config edit path chosen by the user. Everything was reverted to a clean state (Service restored to pod endpoints, public API back to prior VF-backed behavior). NEEDS: a decision on how to repoint OmniRoute's embedding provider (admin API vs DB edit), and whether to also move omniroute off gremlin-1 or just use the direct host URL. NOTE: the OLD VF-path blocker below still stands for the in-cluster pods, but PF-direct host serving is the chosen path forward and it works. ORIGINAL VF ROOT CAUSE: PRIMARY outage root cause is a host-level Intel i915 SR-IOV GPU compute hang on Meteor Lake Arc VFs, NOT a probe/memory/ceiling problem. The embeddings-only sustained-compute workload wedges the VF compute command streamer (ccs0): dmesg floods 'GT0: Unexpected memirq status 0x0 from ccs0' and GPU fences time out ('Fence expiration time out ... ovms[...]'), hanging the serving path after a short healthy window. This reproduces across gremlin-2 (VF 00:02.3) and gremlin-3 (VF 00:02.6), independent of pod revision/probe/memory. A durable kernel-param fix was authored, committed+pushed (nixos-k3s-configs dev 152b4a2), and applied to gremlin-2 (i915.reset=1 full-GPU-reset + i915.request_timeout_ms=10000). RESULT: materially better but INSUFFICIENT — it eliminated fence timeouts (0 since boot) and the permanent-wedge-forever behavior, but the ccs0 memirq storm persists and compute still hangs intermittently for long stretches under load (a 20-call paced in-pod test on fixed gremlin-2 still failed ~10+ consecutive calls). So AC2 (20 consecutive clean /v1/embeddings calls) is NOT met. The remaining root cause is a GuC-compute-submission defect on MTL SR-IOV VFs at the driver/firmware layer; the next remediation (i915-sriov-dkms revision bump, GuC/HuC firmware bump, or disabling GuC-submission/SR-IOV) is a larger, uncertain, higher-regression-risk change to the live 4-node cluster. STOPPED before rebooting gremlin-3/gremlin-4 so three nodes stay on known-prior behavior; gremlin-2 is strictly no-worse (no fence timeouts). Needs a joint decision on the deeper GPU remediation (DKMS/firmware bump + maintenance window) OR an architectural change (e.g. CPU target_device, which the user has so far declined).
findings: FINAL (2026-10-09): embeddings moved HOST-NATIVE to the PF Arc device on all 4 gremlins (shared NixOS module modules/ovms-embeddings-host.nix via common.nix; podman; /dev/dri/renderD128; host :8000; max_length=8192; runtime-resolved video GID; commits 4b2a931+260de4a on branch dev). i915.reset=1 + request_timeout_ms=10000 active fleet-wide (all 4 rebooted; commit 152b4a2). In-cluster ovms-embeddings STS SCALED TO 0 (reversible).
